output.reason: 68-year-old man with two weeks of worsening bilateral ankle swelling and two nights of orthopnea requires immediate emergency assessment for decompensated heart failure, which needs oxygen saturation, chest imaging and bloodwork not obtainable by message.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. Worsening swelling in both ankles plus needing to sit up to breathe at night can mean your heart or lungs are struggling with fluid, and that needs same-hour oxygen checks, imaging and blood tests. Have someone drive you rather than driving yourself. If you develop chest pain, severe breathlessness at rest, or feel faint, call 911 immediately.
differential: Decompensated heart failure with pulmonary congestion
Other systemic fluid retention (kidney or liver cause)
